components.gap: Reconstruct the source's definitions and complete arguments where the route falls short: (1) Definition 8(a)'s clause that a relevance measure's value range is a subinterval, proper or improper, of the extended reals R u {-inf, +inf} (p. 269) is omitted from the reconstruction of Transparency (rationality-4-3.tex 172-180). (2) The Linda argument's representativeness step (p. 273) is omitted: E was designed to be 'representative' of F and 'unrepresentative' of B, and many probabilists would explicate representativeness of a property Phi by the relevance of 'Linda is Phi' to the reference description E, F being positive and B negative to E; the handbook's model (lines 483-500) computes relevance in the direction E-to-target without stating the source's direction. (3) The raven argument (pp. 271-272) is not reconstructed in full: the statement of the paradox through a deductivist criterion that treats logical equivalents H and G alike, so that B (and, with mild further assumptions, C) would support H, which is counterintuitive; the source's step (3) that G is entailed and thereby supported by C ('a is a white shoe'), which the handbook corrects at lines 419-423 without reporting it; and the conclusion that B's merely negligible positive relevance explains the pretheoretical intuition that B, and C in the augmented story, are irrelevant to H. All theorems, lemmas and the other definitions (Definitions 1-7 and 9) are present with written proofs.

Present the source's remaining claims with their claim type and boundaries: (1) Linda (p. 273): the source's historical and empirical report that the conjunction fallacy arose most famously in this late-1970s example, presented on an experimental instruction sheet, and that a surprisingly large proportion of respondents ranked BF above B, contravening P(BF|E) <= P(B|E), is not stated; the route gives only the ranking task and a general note that no counts are supplied, so the empirical claim is not retained with its task, population, design and uncertainty boundary. (2) The source's empirical claim that there is evidence that delta-p = P(H|E) - P(H|~E) serves as an explication of participants' assessments of the relevance of E for H (Skovgaard-Olsen, Singmann and Klauer 2016b) is reduced to 'research including delta-p' (lines 513-521) and is not stated as an empirical claim with its boundary. (3) Omitted evaluative, descriptive and scope claims: extreme valuation 'pleases anyone to whom conclusive argument is the strongest argument'; intuitions on amount symmetry are strong only for asymmetric extreme positivity, and Q's equal values in the divisibility example are something 'many will balk at, because it ignores the entailment asymmetry'; the section 5.6 homomorphism framing (homomorphisms essential to predictability of many ordinal and all quantitative relevance properties of logical complexes; most conditional constraints not practically useful; not all homomorphisms desirable) (all p. 272); that the same relevance relations obtain between statements about past events and between possible experimental results and timeless scientific hypotheses (p. 265); and the summary's description of the task-relative ordinal-equivalence conditions and the disjunctive-evidence properties as two extensions of the state of the art (p. 265). The source's other examples are present.
